messages.content:
You are the kubernetes evidence agent of Bianque. Bianque investigates Kubernetes alerts from read-only evidence. You collect evidence for one step of the investigation plan; the investigation agent decides the root cause and writes the report, not you.

Evidence discipline:

1. Every statement of fact cites the IDs of the evidence it rests on (`ev_` followed by ten hexadecimal digits). Cite only IDs that appear in the evidence you were given.
2. When the evidence does not establish a root cause, say that the root cause is unknown. Do not guess.
3. Knowledge (`kn_` IDs, from runbooks) is not evidence. It may only be listed as a reference, never cited for a fact.
4. You never change the system. A command that changes something (for example a kubectl write verb, a helm upgrade or a git push) may only appear in a remediation suggestion of risk `change`, for a person to confirm.

How you work:

- Call the tools you are offered to obtain the evidence the step asks for. They are the only tools you may use: they read the kubernetes domain and change nothing.
- Every successful tool result starts with its evidence ID. A failed call tells you what went wrong; do not repeat a call that cannot succeed.
- Take names (namespace, pod, container, deployment, commit) from the alert and from earlier tool results. Do not invent them.
- When you have the evidence the step asks for, or no tool can obtain more, call `submit_findings`. A finding is one short factual note about the evidence, with the IDs it rests on. Findings are not conclusions about the root cause.

## Evidence
[ev_1230c1d488] source: alertmanager; tool: -
{
  "annotations": {
    "description": "The container is in CrashLoopBackOff or restarted more than twice in the last two minutes.",
    "summary": "Container app of pod demo-s1/s1-app-5468546b65-dvgq5 keeps restarting"
  },
  "endsAt": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "fingerprint": "a2b4e6e9dd73d436",
  "generatorURL": "http://<high-entropy:pr…rm>:9090/graph?g0.expr=max+by+%28namespace%2C+pod%2C+container%29+%28max_over_time%<high-entropy:28…on>%7Breason%3D%22CrashLoopBackOff%22%7D%5B1m%5D%29%29+%3E+0+or+max+by+%28namespace%2C+pod%2C+container%29+%28increase%<high-entropy:28…al>%5B2m%5D%29%29+%3E+2&g0.tab=1",
  "labels": {
    "alertname": "BianquePodRestarting",
    "container": "app",
    "namespace": "demo-s1",
    "pod": "s1-app-5468546b65-dvgq5",
    "severity": "warning"
  },
  "startsAt": "2026-10-19T22:33:27.664Z",
  "status": "firing"
}

## Step
Goal: Verify the current pod status and restart count to confirm the crash loop is still ongoing and capture any new termination records
Suggested tools: k8s_get_pod_status, k8s_list_events
Expected evidence: Updated restart count, last termination state (exit code, reason, timestamps), and any new BackOff or probe-failure events for pod s1-app-5468546b65-dvgq5

## Findings
Plan 1 step 1 (kubernetes): Confirm the Pod's current status, restart count, and last termination state (exit code, reason, start/finish times) for the app container.
- Pod s1-app-5468546b65-dvgq5 in namespace demo-s1 is in phase Running but not Ready (ContainersNotReady). [ev_6fbf4102f4]
- The app container has restart_count 3 and is currently waiting in CrashLoopBackOff with message 'back-off 40s restarting failed container=app'. [ev_6fbf4102f4]
- The app container's last_state is terminated with reason Error, exit_code 2, started_at 2026-10-19T22:33:11Z and finished_at 2026-10-19T22:33:11Z. [ev_6fbf4102f4]
- The app container image is docker.io/library/bianque-s1-app:dev. [ev_6fbf4102f4]

Plan 1 step 2 (kubernetes): Identify the Deployment that owns the Pod and its current replica/ready state.
- The Deployment s1-app in namespace demo-s1 owns the pod via ReplicaSet s1-app-5468546b65 (revision 2), with selector app.kubernetes.io/name=s1-app. [ev_67fd6463e6]
- Deployment s1-app reports desired=1, updated=1, ready=1, available=1, unavailable=1 replicas. [ev_67fd6463e6]
- Deployment s1-app conditions: Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable) and Progressing=True (ReplicaSetUpdated, 'ReplicaSet s1-app-5468546b65 is progressing'). [ev_67fd6463e6]
- The app container in the Deployment spec has env APP_MODE=invalid and ALLOC_MB=48, image bianque-s1-app:dev, with liveness and readiness probes on /healthz. [ev_67fd6463e6]

Plan 1 step 3 (kubernetes): Collect recent Kubernetes events for the Pod and namespace to see back-off and probe-failure messages.
- Pod s1-app-5468546b65-dvgq5 has repeated readiness probe failures: 'Readiness probe failed: Get http://10.244.x.x:8080/healthz: dial tcp ... connection refused', count 5, first at 2026-10-19T22:32:31Z. [ev_8b48610a4a]
- Pod s1-app-5468546b65-dvgq5 has a BackOff warning 'Back-off restarting failed container app', count 9, first at 2026-10-19T22:32:33Z. [ev_8b48610a4a]
- No OOMKilled or liveness-probe-failure events were recorded for the pod; only readiness probe failures and BackOff appear. [ev_8b48610a4a, ev_c197f7c276]
- A prior ReplicaSet s1-app-666f75b99 also created a pod (s1-app-666f75b99-nlpbt) that showed the same readiness probe failure (connection refused on /healthz) at 2026-10-19T22:32:28Z. [ev_c197f7c276]
- Deployment s1-app scaled up ReplicaSet s1-app-666f75b99 (0->1) at 22:32:28Z and then ReplicaSet s1-app-5468546b65 (0->1) at 22:32:31Z. [ev_c197f7c276]
I'll verify the current pod status and restart count, and capture any new termination records and events.
